title: Ordinary news, jokes, gossip, television, and everyday talk in the dying room

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source utterance/listening-layer synthesis for schema testing; no private testimony, no contributor interview, no claim of corpus completeness.
limitations: Public sources describe communication patterns and response guidance but do not supply consented verbatim bedside testimony.
This record must not become a prophecy, last-words trope, spiritual proof, diagnosis, countdown, or mandatory script.
Treatment, legal, ritual, emergency, and safety decisions remain local and must be handled by qualified teams or relevant authorities.

moment.plain_scene: The room contains ordinary speech: family news, gossip, jokes, sports, television, repeated small talk, or the familiar conversational style the person had before illness.
ordinary_language_queries: can I joke with hospice patient
what to say when there is nothing to say
talk about normal things at end of life

content_layers.observation_text: The archive needs this record because a corpus of dramatic final words would erase how much dying-room language is ordinary, repetitive, practical, funny, or quiet.
content_layers.source_synthesis: Marie Curie and Cancer Council NSW both support ordinary conversation and treating the person as themselves; NHS inform also names telling news from friends and family or playing favorite music when a person may still hear.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: Utterance records should preserve what was heard, who heard it, and what interpretive frames were available without deciding meaning for the family or turning speech into a rule.

what_this_is_not: not trivial just because it is ordinary
not a rule that joking is always appropriate
not a replacement for direct conversation if the person wants directness
uncertainties: Humor can comfort or harm depending on history and culture.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A lay surface should make ordinary talk permissible without saying it is always welcome. It should invite the listener to follow the person's lead and energy.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: A practitioner surface should document how ordinary talk, humor, and television/music preserve personhood, and when they may exhaust, exclude, or disturb the person.
language_notes: Keep the banal; it is part of the truth.
Avoid making the dying room only sacred or tragic.

provenance.provenance_statement: Drafted from named public sources to test the utterance layer. It should be reviewed before any public surface uses it.

safety.clinical_boundary: This record is observational/source-indexing only. It is not medical advice, not a prognosis, not a legal instruction, not a ritual authority, not proof of spiritual meaning, not a diagnosis of delirium, and not a substitute for a local hospice, clinician, emergency, legal, cultural, or care team.
safety.safety_notes: Before public use, route through clinical or domain review and ensure any lay surface directs urgent distress, safety, medication, confusion, swallowing, legal, or crisis concerns to qualified local support.
